rationale:
The `habeas-refactor` skill (`assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md`) directs each obligation in its Workflow, and `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_refactor_skill_moves_first_then_updates_evidence_with_habeas_refactor]` checks them in order.

| Obligation | Where the skill carries it out |
|---|---|
| Make the move with the agent's own edits, kept separate from any change to the moved code or text | Step 1 says "Make the move with your own edits … Change nothing else in this step" and to keep the moved text exactly as it was. Step 7 says to commit "before any change to behavior or text". The Gotchas section repeats "Move first, run the command, commit, then edit." |
| Run `habeas refactor --dry-run` with a mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name | Step 3 asks for one `--map <old>=<new>` for every moved file or directory, node, and definition name. It shows the three forms of `requirements.refactor.mappings`: path, `file#selector`, and definition name with its descendants. |
| Review the report, including records left unchanged and the rationale spans it lists | Step 4 covers "Would rewrite", "Would change" (records updated, with each code span in their rationales that still mentions an old path), and "Would leave … unchanged" (records a mapping affects that fail a check). |
| Run it without `--dry-run` | Step 5. |
| Confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records are stale | Step 6. |
| Commit the move and evidence update before changing behavior | Step 7. |
| Then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the habeas-evidence skill | Step 8 says "Next, reassess what remains stale with `habeas author --all`, following the habeas-evidence skill". |

**Test.** The test uses `assert_in_order` on the bundled skill text. That text is whitespace-collapsed, so phrases that wrap across lines in the markdown still match. The asserted phrases follow the skill's step order and correspond to each row above, including the unchanged-records and rationale-span review phrases. The test carries the `{test}` reference to the subject.

**Unspecified behavior.** Step 2 (stage the move in the Git index) and the `--force` hint in step 4 are extra advice. They support the required commands and add no behavior the requirement leaves out, so I did not count them as gaps. The requirement's cited parts (`requirements.refactor.dry_run`, `requirements.refactor.mappings`, `requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`) are reflected in the skill's instructions.

I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} refactor_skill.workflow
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
:::{req} dry_run
With `--dry-run`, `habeas refactor` MUST report every change it would make,
in the same form as {cite}`requirements.refactor.command`, and MUST write
nothing.
:::{req} mappings
Each `--map` MUST have one of these forms:
- a file or directory path, which maps that file, or every file under that
directory, to the same relative path under the new side;
- `<file>#<selector>`, which maps one outline node, and its outline
descendants, to the node at the new file and selector;
- a definition name, which maps that full name, and every full name beginning
with it followed by `.`, to the same suffix under the new name.
A mapping whose old side names a recorded definition, or a prefix of one
followed by `.`, MUST be a definition-name mapping.
:::{req} rationale.untouched
`habeas refactor` MUST NOT change rationale text other than the spans
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.names`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.paths`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.addresses` cover. For each changed
record, it MUST list the other code spans in the rationale that contain an old
side of a path or node mapping, so the user can review them.
